copy.blurb:
A +13.7pp gap on the France side. Norway v France in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has France stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Elo numbers going in: Norway 1760, France 2030. That's a 270-point lead for France — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 15%, the draw at 14%, and France to win at 71%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 18%, the draw at 22%, and France to win at 57%. On the France side specifically the market reads 57%, which prices out at American odds of −135. Compared against the model's 71%, that's the +13.7pp gap the Pick rests on.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On France, that haircut lands the model at 64%; the market is at 57%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.3pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 36 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives France a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

copy.summary: On every meaningful read, France look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 71% vs market 57% — a +13.7pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Norway v France · the model leans France
